exposure: history of at least 5 epileptic seizures during pregnancy
cohort: Pregnant women (37-41 weeks gestation) divided into three groups: 1) with generalized tonic-clonic epilepsy and at least 5 seizures during pregnancy (n=27), 2) with generalized tonic-clonic epilepsy and no seizures during pregnancy (n=28), and 3) without epilepsy (control group, n=50)
finding: While not statistically significant, pregnant women with a history of 5 or more seizures during pregnancy tended to have lower umbilical arterial blood pH and pO2 values, and higher pCO2 values, compared to those without seizures and the control group.
